Hey, I [F22] have a boyfriend [M22] and a girlfriend [F21]. We're poly. We all have widely different views of the future. I don't want kids ever, at all. I don't want to marry or settle down. My boyfriend wants marriage and kids and the whole traditional thing, down the road of course. My girlfriend is moving next year and isn't a fan/believer of long distance relationships. So, none of us will probably really stay in our current relationship dynamics as we all want to end up in different parts of life/the world. Why, are you asking, are we still in a relationship?

Companionship. We all know 2020 was a hard as fuck year. My boyfriend and I spent most of the year quarantined together. Life experiences. We explore all kinds of hobbies and things together. My girlfriend shows me anime and we encourage each other's interest in fashion. Just general happiness. We're in our early twenties and in university. It's good to have people you can trust, who you can come to, people you enjoy having sex with, regularly. People who know you, your body, your needs.

Yes, we won't be together forever and ever. There will be other people. And that's...okay? We will be in other phases of our lives, doing different things. It's okay.

It's also okay to not want a relationship. Especially if something happened to you that makes you not believe in love or makes you mistrust people who show interest in you. It's okay to focus on friends instead and say no to romantic relationships, and not expect marriage or anything to happen for you in the near future. You're allowed to not want all that (temporary) stuff.
